tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded steps navigate to a WordPress post, locate the standard comment form, fill fields (comment, author, email, url), optionally toggle the 'save my name/email/website' checkbox, submit, and verify the comment appears (anchored). The run produced element hashes and confirmed standard WP ids: #comment, #author, #email, #url, input#wp-comment-cookies-consent, #submit.

Task Definition:
- Build a re-usable, deterministic tool to post a comment to a WordPress post URL using provided values for comment, author, email, and optional website, with optional cookie-consent toggling and verification that the comment appears.

Action Plan:
1. Navigate to provided post_url.
2. Wait briefly for page/scripts to initialize and confirm the comment form exists.
3. Fill the comment textarea (#comment) with {comment}.
4. Fill name (#author), email (#email), and website (#url) fields.
5. Conditionally toggle cookie-consent checkbox only when {wp_comment_cookies_consent} is true. Use an agent step to perform this conditional action robustly (handles variations in id/name and avoids unconditional clicks).
6. Click the submit control (prefer #submit or submit control within form#commentform).
7. Wait for server processing and page reload/anchor, then extract page content to verify that a comment by {author} containing the comment text appears.

Variable Identification:
- post_url: target page to navigate (required).
- comment: comment text -> maps to textarea name/id 'comment' (required).
- author: commenter display name -> maps to input name/id 'author' (required).
- email: commenter email -> maps to input name/id 'email' (required).
- url: optional website -> maps to input name/id 'url' (optional).
- wp_comment_cookies_consent: boolean indicating whether to check cookie-consent checkbox (optional).

Step Optimization & Determinism:
- Navigation uses direct URL rather than UI clicks (more deterministic).
- Form inputs use stable WP ids (#comment, #author, #email, #url) with elementHash recorded as a fallback for deterministic targeting.
- The cookie checkbox is conditional; to avoid non-deterministic unconditional clicks, an agent step is used to inspect the page and perform the toggle only when requested, while using robust selector fallbacks (id, name contains 'cookies', label-relative). This follows the rule to prefer deterministic selectors but use agentic logic for conditional/dynamic interactions.
- Submission uses the common #submit selector and scoped form submit controls to avoid clicking unrelated submit buttons.
- Verification uses an extraction step looking for author text and a snippet of the comment to determine success; exact comment id may vary so the verification looks for visible evidence rather than assuming a fixed id.

Failure Modes & Mitigations:
- If the page returns an error or redirects to a login, the initial extract_page_content will surface that and the tool caller can detect failure via the 'initial_form_check' output.
- If preferred selectors are missing or duplicated, the agent step and extraction steps will log which selector matched; callers should implement retry/retry-with-snapshot strategies if needed.

Notes:
- The agent is assumed to already be authenticated if required; no auth steps are included.
- Required fields match visible form indicators (Comment*, Name*, Email*). 'url' is optional.
- The tool intentionally avoids branching in the main step list; conditional checkbox handling is delegated to a bounded 'agent' step to adhere to the system's requirement for robust conditional actions.
name: tool_post_comment.v3
description: Submit a WordPress post comment programmatically. Navigates to a post URL, fills the standard WP comment form (comment, author, email, website), optionally toggles the 'save my name/email/website' checkbox, submits the comment, and verifies the new comment appears on the page.

steps.description: Navigate directly to the post URL where the comment form is located.
Brief pause to allow page scripts and the comment form to initialize.
Capture page content and confirm comment form is present. This helps detect redirects or missing form.
steps.goal: Confirm presence of core comment form selectors (#comment, #author, #email, #url or their fallbacks) before filling.

steps.description: Enter the comment text into the textarea (preferred selector: #comment).
Enter the commenter display name into the name field (preferred selector: #author).
Enter the commenter email into the email field (preferred selector: #email).
Enter the optional website/URL into the url field. Pass an empty string to leave blank.
Agentic step to conditionally toggle the cookie-consent checkbox. Agent reasoning is used to avoid unconditional clicks and to robustly select the checkbox if the id differs.
steps.task: If {wp_comment_cookies_consent} is true, locate the cookie consent checkbox (preferred selector: input#wp-comment-cookies-consent or input[type='checkbox'][name*='cookies' i]) and click it once. If false or the selector is not found, do nothing. Log which selector was used or if skipped.

steps.description: Click the comment submit control (preferred selector: #submit or the submit control inside form#commentform).
Wait for the server to process the submission and for the page to reload/anchor to the new comment.
Extract verification evidence (e.g., li#comment-<id>, visible author text, and comment snippet) to confirm successful submission.
steps.goal: Verify that the comment by '{author}' with the text starting with the first 40 characters of '{comment}' appears on the page (look for author text and snippet or li#comment-*).

input_schema.name: post_url
input_schema.description: Full URL of the post page to comment on (example: 'http://localhost:8000/?p=8'). The tool will navigate to this URL.

input_schema.name: comment
input_schema.description: The comment text to submit. This maps to the WordPress 'comment' textarea (id/name 'comment').

input_schema.name: author
input_schema.description: Display name for the comment (maps to input id/name 'author'). Required by most WP installs.

input_schema.name: email
input_schema.description: Email address for the comment (maps to input id/name 'email'). Required by most WP installs.

input_schema.name: url
input_schema.description: Optional website/URL for the commenter (maps to input id/name 'url'). Provide full URL e.g. 'https://example.com' or empty string to skip.

input_schema.name: wp_comment_cookies_consent
input_schema.description: If true, the tool will enable the 'Save my name, email, and website in this browser' checkbox (input#wp-comment-cookies-consent). Default false.
